PullRequest.Title: test: interrupt async operations at every step, and fix leaks after await
PullRequest.Body:
Based on #346261 (lint rule `local/code-no-register-after-await`). Review only the top commit.

**`interruptAtEveryStep` test helper** (`src/vs/base/test/common/interruptAtEveryStep.ts`)

It starts an async operation and interrupts it after 0, 1, 2, � steps, until a run completes before it is interrupted, so every `await` gets interrupted once. After each run it fails, naming the step, if:
- disposables leaked
- an unexpected error occurred
- the operation didn't settle

Steps are microtask hops by default. Pass `step: 'macrotask'` for operations that wait on timers or I/O. Supporting changes:
- `getDisposableTracker()` in `lifecycle.ts`
- the virtual-time processor now owns its park subscription

New tests for storage init and terminal process startup use the helper. They fail when the fixes for #345627 and #340582 are reverted.

**Leak fixes.** These now re-check disposal after an `await`, and their files are removed from the baseline:
- chat debug detail panel and wire log view
- MCP app model
- comment node, reply, thread widget and zone widget
- notebook sticky scroll
- mission control environment service

Also adds a "Disposal During Async Work" section to `writing-tests.instructions.md`.

Originally by @alexdima.

**Validation**
- `scripts/test.bat` on the lifecycle, interruptAtEveryStep, storageMainService, terminalProcess and missionControlEnvironmentService tests: 112 passing, 2 pending (live terminal tests are skipped on Windows)
- `pnpm run eslint` on the changed files: clean

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: CommentReply could be disposed while createModelReference was pending; when the promise resolved, the old code registered the reference with an already-disposed DisposableStore. DisposableStore.add explicitly does not retain or dispose such an item, so the model reference and underlying text model were leaked.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Rapidly closing a comment thread while its reply model resolves could retain one model reference and text model per race, producing disposal-leak failures and cumulative workbench memory growth.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: After model creation resolves, the new disposed-state check immediately disposes the model reference and returns instead of registering it into a dead owner.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The changed branch at RIGHT line 101 calls model.dispose() when this._store.isDisposed. The prior continuation reached base line 102, this._register(model), after the await; lifecycle.ts documents and implements that add on a disposed store leaks the added object. createModelReference is reference-counted by TextModelResolverService, so failing to dispose the returned reference retains the model. Blame identifies the commit that introduced that registration.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The edit model reference could resolve after CommentNode disposal. The old continuation then added that reference to an already-disposed edit-mode store, whose add operation warns but neither owns nor disposes the object, leaking the reference-counted text model.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Closing a comment or editor while comment-edit model creation was pending could retain a model and its buffers per occurrence, causing cumulative memory/GC pressure.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new disposed-state branch disposes modelRef immediately and stops the continuation before assigning or registering the model.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: RIGHT line 488 is the newly added modelRef.dispose() on the post-await disposal path. Before the PR, execution continued to the registration represented by base line 489; DisposableStore.add's implementation confirms an already-disposed store leaks the object, and TextModelResolverService returns a reference-counted model handle. Blame identifies the introducing commit.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: NotebookStickyScroll could be disposed while computeFullSymbols was pending. Its dispose method disposes _disposables, but the old continuation then added outline/editor/scroll listeners to that dead store; DisposableStore.add leaves such listeners undisposed, allowing event emitters to retain the sticky-scroll object.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Closing a notebook during asynchronous symbol computation could retain sticky-scroll listeners and their UI/model closure, accumulating memory and future callback work.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new post-computation disposed check returns before content creation and all listener registrations.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: RIGHT line 217 checks this._store.isDisposed immediately after computeFullSymbols. The old path continued to base line 222, the first _disposables listener registration; the class dispose method disposes _disposables before super.dispose, and lifecycle.ts confirms subsequent add calls leak rather than self-dispose. Blame resolves the commit that introduced this post-await listener setup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Async interruption test helper exercised by in-memory storage initialization and terminal process startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: This is test-only. interruptAtEveryStep serially starts, advances, interrupts, settles, and cleans one run before the next; it is not on product startup. The terminal test's final successful run must complete filesystem validation and process startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: TerminalProcess validates cwd and executable and may inspect/copy shell-integration files during start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One validation sequence per helper run until startup completes; runs are serial and the added test has a 500-step hard cap. Early interrupted runs are expected to stop before spawn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The startup implementation already performed these filesystem operations, but this exhaustive interruption test did not invoke it repeatedly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Filesystem completion determines each macrotask-stepped test run's progress; it affects test duration only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn the test terminal's Node process through node-pty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The test asserts every interrupted run has zero spawn attempts; only the non-interrupted completion run reaches one spawn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing targeted terminal tests spawned fixtures, but this interruption test and its single successful spawn were absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The final run waits for startup, then immediately cleans up the fixture; no subprocess fan-out or product-path impact is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of asynchronous steps S controls S+1 serial reruns and roughly quadratic step advances in the generic helper, bounded by maxSteps=500; the two added integrations have short initialization paths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly one run is active at a time; no Promise.all across runs. Terminal cwd/executable validation is internally parallel as before, and subprocess creation is not concurrent across runs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new product cache. Each test run creates fresh fixtures; terminal executable/filesystem caches, if any, are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the helper loop, serial awaits, hard cap, terminal filesystem calls, and spawn guard were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact test duration depends on host filesystem and node-pty startup, but the process count is asserted and the helper is bounded and test-only.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The exhaustive repetition is deliberate, bounded test work; it neither enters product execution nor creates a subprocess burst.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening, editing, and rapidly closing comment threads while comment input models resolve
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Comment UI initialization awaits one createModelReference before wiring the editor and listeners. The PR adds only a disposed-state branch after that existing await; normal initialization latency is unchanged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One unique comments-input model reference per reply or edit UI; raced closures scale with user-opened comment widgets, not comment collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each widget has its own asynchronous acquisition; the diff adds no scheduling or aggregate concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: TextModelResolverService reference-counts models by canonical URI. Reply/edit resources are generally unique, and the new branch releases the acquired reference when its owner died.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: DisposableStore.add explicitly leaks objects added after disposal, while the changed branches dispose the returned references.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of users closing during model acquisition is unknown, but the leak mechanism and cleanup are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance improvement, not a regression. The PR prevents retained model references and associated memory/GC pressure; corresponding regression fixes were recorded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Loading chat debug details and wire-log sources, and completing MCP app initialization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detail rendering awaits provider resolution/rendering; wire-log loading awaits source enumeration; MCP initialization awaits its existing notification. Added checks only stop continuations after owner disposal and are off the successful-path cost beyond a boolean read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a debug event through registered providers, sequentially until one returns content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one call per provider for one selected event; the PR does not change provider count or invocation frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same sequential provider resolution completed before rendering; disposed panels could continue allocating UI afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing event-detail critical path; the new post-await guard prevents rendering after disposal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List available local or remote agent-host wire-log files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped log-directory enumeration per wire-log load, not one call per source; source filtering follows in memory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same enumeration ran once, followed by UI setup even when the view had been disposed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing wire-log load boundary; the added guard avoids control/listener construction after disposal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the MCP tool-input notification to the app view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One delayed notification per app initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The notification was already sent and awaited; a disposed model could then retain an autorun or send a result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited initialization message; the new check suppresses only subsequent result subscription/sends after disposal.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected debug event, one session log directory, or one app initialization respectively; no collection-wide operation moved into a per-item loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Debug providers are sequential; log enumeration is one grouped operation; the MCP callback awaits one notification. The diff adds no concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache keys or cache lifecycle changed. Existing source discovery and provider behavior are preserved on live views.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all boundaries predate the diff and the changed checks only cut off dead-owner continuations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider and remote filesystem latency varies, but boundary cardinality and unchanged placement are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The changes prevent post-disposal DOM/listener/autorun retention and do not add expensive calls or fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connecting to a Mission Control environment while the environment service is disposed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Connection already awaited service initialization before host lookup, environment/account network reads, and remote connect. The new check aborts immediately after initialization if the owner was disposed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize environment inventory, fetch environment/account state, and establish or recover the remote connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: connect coalesces one pending promise per environment id; after initialization, one environment read, one account read, and at most one connect/disconnect sequence occur.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A disposal during initialize could continue into host/API/connection work; the PR now cancels before those calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing calls are on the user-requested connection path. The changed check removes them from the disposed-service path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct requested environment IDs after per-ID pending-connect coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Calls for the same ID share _pendingConnects; different IDs may proceed independently as before. The diff only suppresses a dead-owner continuation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Host inventory may be cached/persisted as before; no cache key, invalidation, or negative-cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the guard is immediately before all post-initialize network/connection work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote latency and frequency of disposal races vary, but the eliminated boundary path is directly traced.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance improvement, not a regression; disposal now prevents unnecessary remote work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Notebook sticky-scroll initialization while symbol computation is pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sticky-scroll initialization already awaited full symbol computation before computing visible content and registering outline, view-model, and scroll listeners. The new disposed check skips all downstream work for a closed notebook.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute full notebook symbols, potentially invoking language-feature providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One computation per sticky-scroll initialization; later attach events retain their existing behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same symbol computation ran, then the continuation registered listeners even if dispose had already disposed their store.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing initialization boundary. The PR does not add or repeat it, but prevents rendering/listener setup after disposal.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Notebook cell/symbol count controls the existing computation and content-map size; the changed constant-time check does not alter scaling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new parallelism; one init continuation per invocation, with existing configuration-triggered calls unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The outline factory's getOrCreate/reference lifecycle is unchanged; the new branch leaves the already-owned reference to normal class disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: class disposal disposes _disposables, and old post-await add calls leaked listeners according to DisposableStore semantics.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Symbol-provider latency and notebook size vary, but listener retention on the disposal race is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance improvement, not a regression. It prevents retained notebook UI/listeners and downstream rendering after closure; the regression fix was recorded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Virtual-time processor parking and disposal in test infrastructure
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A parked processor subscribes to clock scheduling. Replacing the raw field with a registered MutableDisposable keeps wake/unpark behavior unchanged while making class disposal own the active subscription.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active park subscription per processor regardless of scheduled-event count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Wake calls remain macrotask-coalesced; the diff does not increase scheduled callbacks or parallelism.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership and disposal paths are explicit in the changed class.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Only test infrastructure is affected; retained processor lifetime depended on whether disposal occurred while parked.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The change closes a one-subscription lifecycle leak without adding repeated work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 18 changed files and every diff page. No actionable performance regression was introduced, so no findings were submitted. The PR predominantly removes cleanup-lifecycle leaks and dead-owner boundary work; three concrete shipped leak fixes were recorded for regression learning.
